gap: No result ChatGPT got states today's price and stock for the whole 240 V field: BLUETTI Apex 300 is $1,499 and in stock, Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus is $3,499 on pre-order shipping Nov 28, a 240 V Growatt HELIOS 3600 pair with hub is $2,536.96, and the Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus that ChatGPT priced at $2,999.99 shows Sold Out on Anker's own page.
standout_why: Compared against willitrunpower.com, homebatteryreport.com and grid.ceo, all opened 2026-11-11. Willrun already gives price and stock for ChatGPT's two picks (DELTA Pro 3 $2,799 with the standalone unit unavailable, F3800 Plus $2,999.99 sold out) and locked-rotor margins per pump size. Home Battery Report already has the pick-deciding surge facts (F3800 Plus 80 A LRA, Jackery 14,400 W, Apex 300 with no motor surge figure) but lists no prices. grid.ceo gives only price ranges for three models. None prices Apex 300, Jackery 5000 Plus, Growatt HELIOS 3600, Sun Gold Power SGR-8K10E, OSCAL PowerMax 6000 or Anker S5000, and none gives the Jackery ship date. offsprig.com (rank 1) and wellwaterauthority.com failed to load (certificate error), so I could not check whether they already carry prices; that keeps this at 1 rather than 2.
decides: It confirms the pick logic rather than changing it: price does not rescue the cheap 240 V units. Apex 300 at $1,499 is the cheapest in-stock 120/240 V single unit, but 3,840 W is 16 A at 240 V and Home Battery Report found no motor-start surge figure for it. The one station with a published watt surge above a 1 HP two-wire pump's 48.7 A locked-rotor draw is the Jackery 5000 Plus (14,400 W, 60 A at 240 V), at $3,499 and not shipping until Nov 28. The F3800 Plus (80 A LRA per Home Battery Report's reading of the user guide) is sold out at Anker today. So a shopper who must buy today is left with the DELTA Pro 3 class (33.3 A surge, 1/2 HP only on paper) or a pre-order.
